root.name: Caro-Kann Defense: Edinburgh Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nd2 Qb6

overview: The Edinburgh is 3.Nd2 Qb6 in the Caro-Kann Modern line: Black hits b2 and d4 with the queen early, and White usually defends with Ngf3 or Nb3, keeping a solid centre. The queen sortie costs time but gives Black some activity. Play is sound and manoeuvring, closer to the Caro-Kann than to the sharp variations.

white_ideas.idea: Defend with Ngf3 or Nb3 and build the centre
Exchange pawns on d5 and open lines

black_ideas.idea: Pressure d4 and b2 with the queen
Support ...dxe4 and ...Bf5 for normal Caro-Kann play

typical_structures.structure: Caro-Kann with Black queen on b6 and exchanges on d5 or e4

character.notes: Black stays flexible while the queen sortie adds some tactical edge.

approach.notes: Less popular than the main lines but respectable.

character.reason: A quiet Caro-Kann sideline whose early queen sortie adds some activity but not forcing play.

structure.reason: The Caro-Kann semi-open structure after exchanges on d5 or e4.

plans.reason: Black's queen comes out early and has to avoid being harassed.
